title: Law Firm Linked to Elon Musk Started an ‘Election Integrity’ Organization
gist: A Musk-linked law firm (Lex Politica) set up a nationwide 'election integrity' nonprofit, the Association of State and Local Election Officials, whose board is stocked with election-denial figures; Musk is the largest GOP donor this cycle with $445 million and has a stake in the midterms outcome.

insights.claim: Elon Musk is the single largest donor to Republican candidates this cycle, spending more than $445 million, including $276 million since July, nearly as much as in the entire 2024 presidential cycle.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: Musk's political exposure is a material factor in his companies' regulatory and political risk.
insights.locator: Musk is the single largest donor to Republican candidates

insights.claim: A Democratic House and Senate majority could expose Musk and his companies to congressional investigations, which explains his heavy midterm spending.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: Midterm results are a regulatory-risk catalyst for Musk-linked companies.
insights.locator: These elections are crucial for Musk

insights.claim: America PAC is financing a large canvassing operation for Republicans in November and has spread inaccurate information about mail-in ballots.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: Watch for platform and legal consequences of election misinformation.
insights.locator: America PAC has also spread inaccurate information

insights.claim: The Association of State and Local Election Officials was registered in Texas on June 17 by Michael Garcar, then a Lex Politica attorney, and received IRS tax-exempt status on July 20.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
entities: Association of State and Local Election Officials
insights.so_what: Shows a fast, low-visibility build of infrastructure for election-policy influence.
insights.locator: The Association of State and Local Election Officials was first registered on June 17

insights.claim: Its registered Washington address is a UPS Store box belonging to Lex Politica, and the group has no web presence or described work in its Texas filing.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: Opacity suggests the group is still a shell ahead of a post-election launch.
insights.locator: The organization's Texas registration contains no information

insights.claim: Florida's Cord Byrd and Governor Ron DeSantis announced the group will use Florida's hard-line election rules as a 'blueprint' nationwide, with state chapters training local election officials.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: Florida-style proof-of-citizenship rules may be exported to other states.
insights.quote: take what we’ve done in Florida as the blueprint, as the model for the nation, take it nationwide

insights.claim: Lex Politica's founder Chris Gober was chief counsel of America PAC and is running for a Texas House seat; Garcar has since moved to Five Rings Law Group, staffed by Lex Politica alumni.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: Maps the personnel network around Musk-aligned political legal work.
insights.locator: Garcar has since left Lex Politica

insights.claim: The board includes Sharon Bemis, president of Cleta Mitchell's Election Integrity Network, plus Georgia's Julie Adams and Janice Johnston and Michigan state representative Ann Bollin, linking the group to the election-denial movement.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: Signals the group will be aligned with Trump's fraud claims rather than neutral.
insights.locator: The organization's board is also staffed by Sharon Bemis

insights.claim: Johnston and Adams targeted Fulton County, and Johnston provided information to an FBI affidavit preceding a January raid that seized tens of thousands of 2020 ballots, despite the double-counting claims having been investigated and shown not to affect the outcome.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: Federal law enforcement has been drawn into re-litigating the 2020 election, a rule-of-law risk.
insights.locator: Johnston was one of the unnamed witnesses

insights.claim: Musk has pushed the great replacement theory and election conspiracies, including a false story about Texas candidate James Talarico, though he has reduced public posting about elections recently.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: His X platform remains a vector for political misinformation.
insights.locator: Musk has continually pushed election conspiracies

insights.claim: Musk's link to the new group is unconfirmed: the article says it is not clear whether he is involved.
insights.speaker: Justin Glawe
insights.so_what: Treat the Musk connection as proximity through his law firm, not confirmed involvement.
insights.quote: It’s not clear if Musk is involved in the organization.
insights.locator: It's not clear if Musk is involved

top_entities: Association of State and Local Election Officials
